paragraphs: For your encoder: 128 observations directly in Python. Use RobotBatch(...).observations() for static simulated scenes or ObservationBatch(...).observations() for fast cached real SO-101 samples. Both return batched RGB images, proprioception, and text; neither includes a model or policy. The examples generate previews and small real-data caches in outputs/.

Two SO-101 follower arms, a table, colored cubes/cylinders, and three cameras (overhead plus one per wrist). Start by reaching a green target; then try picking up the block. Everything runs locally without a learned model.

Match your real camera rig: the camera guide records the Arducam B030401 IMX708 USB modules (the Raspberry Pi Camera Module 3 sensor with autofocus) and covers native 640×480 feeds, wrist attachment, a shared optics/pose profile, lens calibration and remaining transfer differences. Press V in the viewer to cycle all three views, or launch ./play.sh --view overhead. The optics remain nominal until each real camera is calibrated. python scripts/rendersetup.py renders the rig overview in outputs/mujocosetup.png.
